title: Few-shot curation surgepad
summary: Working scratchpad for building compact, robust few-shot sets and template families. Focus: reduce hallucination drift for persona-conditioned replies and improve sample diversity while keeping prompts <= 4 examples.
body:
Purpose / quick notes:
- Short-term goal: produce 3 canonical few-shot families (concise reply, policy-aware reply, extractive-summary) that we can A/B in Hosted API.
- Constraint: prefer 2-4 exemplars; total token add-on < 600 tokens for average user prompt; supports persona conditioning token slot.
- Why: too many current prompt variants overfit to narrow phrasing; models drift into creative hallucination when exemplar diversity is low.

Open hypotheses:
1) Mixing one negative example (shows failure) with two good examples reduces confident hallucination when asked about unverifiable facts.
2) Explicit source-check instruction in each exemplar ("check for source: NONE -> do not fabricate") reduces invented citations but may increase terse answers.
3) Including a short metadata line (role, tone) before each exemplar yields more consistent persona adherence across models and quantized variants.

Priority experiments (ranked):
- P1: Persona-conditioned support reply set (3 variants) -> metric: hallucination rate on synthetic probe (see repro steps).
- P2: Extractive summary few-shot (2 examples + negative) -> metric: F1 vs. ground-truth spans + hallucination incidence.
- P3: Mini-A/B across redwood-hosted/model-variants (fp16/int8/8-bit quant) to check sensitivity to quantization.

Candidate exemplar family: concise-support-reply (3-shot)
-- prompt skeleton: [SYSTEM_INSTR] + [PERSONA_TOKEN] + [EXAMPLES_BLOCK] + [USER_QUERY]

EXAMPLES_BLOCK (Concise family):
1) ---
role: support / tone: concise helpful
Q: "My subscription shows 'cancelled' but I still have access. What gives?"
A: "Looks like billing didn't renew — you still have active sessions but no future billing. Please check Billing > Payment Methods and ping support@redwood with your account ID; we'll restore if charged in error."
2) ---
role: support / tone: concise helpful
Q: "I got duplicated embeddings for the same doc after migration."
A: "Duplicates usually mean the ingestion job retried. Check ingestion logs for duplicate IDs; de-dupe by external_id and re-run the ingestion with dedupe=true. I can share the command if needed."
3) (Negative) ---
role: support / tone: concise helpful
Q: "Is my data used to train models?"
A: "No — we do not use customer data to train public models. If there are special agreements (enterprise on-prem) check contract. If you're seeing a claim otherwise, forward it to legal@redwood."
---
Notes: negative example phrased as factual refusal to fabricate; purpose is to anchor model when uncertain.

Extractive-summary family (2 good + 1 negative):
- Example A: input long chat -> output: three bullet TL;DR capturing actionable items with timestamps. (show exact bullet formatting)
- Example B: same but with embedded code snippet -> show how to include code context extraction
- Negative example: input contains a fictional claim -> expected output: "Cannot verify: [claim]."

Reproduction steps for hallucination probe (quick):
1) Create small probe set of 60 examples: 20 verifiable facts, 20 ambiguous but checkable items, 20 fabricated facts in context.
2) Run baseline prompt (current prod template) vs. new families; measure rate of assertive false statements and presence of invented citations.
3) Instrument streaming output to catch immediate confident assertions (first sentence accuracy).

Failure cases observed (notes to self):
- Model turns negative example into a "warning" and then elaborates anyway. (i.e., the refusal is softened: "I can't verify that, but it *might* be...")
- Template with explicit "do not invent" reduces hallucination but often drops into generic "I don't know" — tradeoff between safety and usefulness.
- Few-shot sets with very similar surface forms across examples cause overfitting; model parrots style but not factuality.

Mitigations to try (quick list):
- Add explicit "if unsure, ask for clarification" instruction in system message to encourage follow-ups.
- Mix synthetic negative examples that demonstrate specific failure modes instead of generic ones.
- Add a short rubric at the end of example outputs (e.g., "SOURCES: none / verified") to teach the format for source claims.

Evaluation heuristics / crude metrics to track:
- Hallucination rate: percent of outputs containing an objectively falsifiable statement not present in input (manual label for first run).
- Brevity score: average token length of first sentence (want balance).
- Persona adherence: binary label whether reply used instructed tone/role.
- Useful-refusal rate: percent of refusals that propose next steps (i.e., "I can't verify, please share X").

Quick A/B run plan (1-day run):
- Select 4 model endpoints: hosted-small, hosted-medium, dedicated-gpu-rtx, private-vpc (local int8).
- Put 60-probe set behind experiment harness. 20 runs each model x prompt family. Capture raw outputs + latency.
- Manual label subset (n=120) for hallucination and persona adherence; automated heuristics for length.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Convert the 60-probe set into a small CSV and attach to Linear ticket AI-789.
- [ ] Draft short PR template for prompt family additions (link example in PR body).
- [ ] Check with SRE about rate limits for burst testing on hosted endpoints (ask @Ethan).
- [ ] Try the negative-example placement: put negative as last example vs first example and compare.

Scratch experiments (ad-hoc results):
- 2026-01-12: small test with negative-last reduced invented citations by ~17% on hosted-medium but increased terse refusals by ~9%.
- 2026-02-04: adding tiny metadata line "role: concise agent" before user query improved persona adherence by coarse heuristic +12%.

Questions / unresolved:
- Does adding an explicit examples-of-bad-output (rather than a single negative) help more than a single negative? (costs tokens)
- Are any of these behaviors heavily model-size dependent (we suspect yes for quantized runs).

Reference snippets to copy into PRs / tests:
- System instruction (compact): "You are a Redwood support agent. Answer concisely, do not invent facts. If you cannot verify, say 'Cannot verify — please provide X.' Keep tone helpful."
- Example negative: "If the question asks about internal audit logs or contract clauses, do not make claims; request the document or escalate to legal."

Slack notes (for quick copy):
- "Heads up: running few-shot A/B today across 4 endpoints. Expect ~500 requests; will throttle if SRE asks. Results will be in Linear AI-789."

Bottom line: keep sets small, diverse, and include at least one concrete negative example that shows the desired refusal style. Next week: run the 1-day A/B and then iterate on negative placement and metadata lines.

-- end of surgepad (notes are messy; clean up for PRs)
